anatomy.flutter: ChartContainer (ChartScope InheritedWidget + SizedBox + DefaultTextStyle + Center) wrapping a plot widget; ChartTooltipContent (header via _label + rows via _row/_indicator); ChartLegendContent (_key per item); ChartConfig/ChartSeries hold label/color/icon per series key.
anatomy.web: ChartContainer (ChartContext.Provider + ChartStyle <style> + ResponsiveContainer) wrapping RechartsPrimitive children; ChartTooltipContent (tooltipLabel + payload.map row); ChartLegendContent (payload.map item); ChartConfig type carries label/icon/color-or-theme per key.

api.flutter: ChartSeries({label, color, icon}) -- `color` is a single resolved Flutter Color, since ChartText/ChartMotion note '--chart-1 ... -5 are already declared once per theme' so no light/dark split is needed at the config level; ChartStyle from the reference is explicitly not ported ('ChartStyle is not ported, and that is the reference's own decision').
api.web: ChartConfig entries carry either {color} or {theme: {light, dark}} plus a <style> tag (ChartStyle) that emits per-theme CSS custom properties --color-<key> so one config can hold two values.
api.note: This is the file's own documented, deliberate platform difference: the web needs a dual light/dark color per series because Tailwind/CSS custom properties are resolved once at build/config time outside the render tree, whereas Flutter resolves ThemeScope.of(context) live on every build, so a ChartSeries.color can be a single Color chosen per-theme by the caller. Recorded as platform-difference per the source's own rationale, not a gap.

states.flutter: ChartMotion documents entrance duration/curve (MotionDurations.slow, MotionCurves.decelerate -- deliberately reproducing recharts' CSS keyword 'ease-out' bug rather than the token's true curve) and effectiveMotionDuration resolves the reduced-motion path; no other interaction state lives in chart.tsx itself (hover/tooltip state belongs to the cartesian/polar plot widgets).
states.web: Recharts' `animationDuration`/`animationEasing` (raw number + CSS keyword string) drive entrance, and `isAnimationActive: false` is the hook's reduced-motion path; hover/active tooltip state lives in the cartesian/polar chart components, not in chart.tsx.

disabled.flutter: ChartContainer/ChartTooltipContent/ChartLegendContent have no disabled concept -- they are presentation primitives for whatever plot is inside them.
disabled.web: No disabled prop exists on ChartContainer, ChartTooltip, or ChartLegend.
disabled.note: Neither side treats a chart as a control that can be disabled; this dimension does not apply to the shared chart chrome.

interaction.flutter: chart.tsx itself (container/tooltip/legend) wires no pointer/keyboard handling directly -- hover and index tracking are owned by CartesianChart/PieChart/RadarChart/RadialBarChart in the sibling files.
interaction.web: ChartContainer/ChartTooltipContent/ChartLegendContent likewise carry no interaction logic of their own; Recharts' own chart components own hover/click.
interaction.note: Interaction is out of scope for this shared-chrome file on both platforms and is audited instead under chart-cartesian and chart-polar.

semantics.flutter: ChartContainer takes no accessible-name / description parameter at all -- it is SizedBox + DefaultTextStyle + Center with no Semantics wrapper, role, or description slot anywhere in the widget.
semantics.web: ChartContainer accepts `description` and reads aria-label/aria-labelledby off props to decide whether to stamp role="img" and wire aria-describedby to a hidden description span -- documented at length in the file's own doc comment as fixing an axe aria-prohibited-attr violation and giving screen readers a real reading of the chart instead of raw axis-tick numbers.
semantics.note: Reclassified on review from `gap`: the shortfall recorded below is on the FLUTTER side — the web has the capability, or Flutter's own doc comment records it as not ported, or Flutter reproduces an earlier state of the web source that has since moved on. This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. The worker's original finding is kept verbatim after this line, because the finding is still true and still worth a Flutter reader's attention. ORIGINAL: This is a genuine accessibility gap, not a platform difference: the web's role=img + aria-describedby(description) pattern is the only way a chart on that page is announced meaningfully to assistive technology, and chart.dart's ChartContainer has no equivalent hook (no Semantics(label:, hint:) parameter, no way for a caller to supply a textual description of the chart's data). Any Flutter screen using ChartContainer today renders an unlabelled picture to a screen reader.
